ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A girl asks another girl maa ismuki? What is she asking? (1 mark)
   A. Where is the book?
   B. How are you?
   C. Who is this?
   D. What is your name?

2. Which Arabic word means "I am well"? (1 mark)
   A. مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ
   B. مَرْحَبًا
   C. أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ
   D. اسْمِي

3. How is the Arabic word أَنَا read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. maʿa s-salaama
   B. sabaahu l-khayr
   C. anaa
   D. as-salaamu ʿalaykum

4. What does the Arabic sentence أَخِي يَلْعَبُ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I have a brother and a sister.
   B. My brother plays.
   C. This is my mother.
   D. This is my father.

5. What does the Arabic word الْأَحَدُ (al-ahad) mean? (1 mark)
   A. Sunday
   B. Tuesday
   C. day
   D. week

6. What is phonological awareness? (1 mark)
   A. Noticing the sounds inside words
   B. Spelling only
   C. Writing quickly
   D. Knowing many words

7. Which Arabic word means "stand up"? (1 mark)
   A. اِقْرَأْ
   B. قِفْ
   C. أَغْلِقِ الْبَابَ
   D. اِسْمَعْ

8. What does the Arabic sentence أَتَكَلَّمُ بِفَمِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I smell with my nose.
   B. I see with my eye.
   C. I hear with my ear.
   D. I speak with my mouth.

9. In the game Simon Says, how do learners show they are listening? (1 mark)
   A. They speak loudly
   B. They cover their ears
   C. They act on every instruction
   D. They act only on the correct instruction

10. What does the Arabic word شَجَرَةٌ (shajara) mean? (1 mark)
   A. cloudy
   B. wind
   C. hot
   D. tree

11. What does the Arabic sentence الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The weather is rainy.
   B. The weather is cloudy.
   C. The weather is hot.
   D. The weather is cold.

12. What does the Arabic sentence فِي بَيْتِي مَطْبَخٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. This is my room.
   B. In my house there is a kitchen.
   C. Thank you for listening.
   D. I am in Grade 4.

13. How do you read the syllable بِ? (1 mark)
   A. bi
   B. nu
   C. bii
   D. tu

14. What is the name of the Arabic letter ا? (1 mark)
   A. alif
   B. Saad
   C. daal
   D. nuun

15. What do the two little strokes at the end of شُكْرًا (shukran) create? (1 mark)
   A. The sound -in
   B. A long ii
   C. The sound -an
   D. The sound -un

16. Which strategy uses a picture or the sentence to guess a word? (1 mark)
   A. Decoding only
   B. Copying
   C. Cues
   D. Clapping

17. Which letters do NOT join to the letter after them? (1 mark)
   A. alif, daal, dhaal, raa, zaay and waaw
   B. siin and shiin
   C. baa, taa and thaa
   D. miim and nuun

18. What does the Arabic sentence مَرْحَبًا يَا أَحْمَدُ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My grandfather is old (big in age).
   B. My brother is small.
   C. Hello, Ahmad.
   D. My sister is beautiful.

19. How is the Arabic word الثُّلَاثَاءُ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. al-ithnayn
   B. usbuuʿ
   C. ath-thulaathaa'
   D. al-khamiis

20. Which Arabic sentence means "I like food." (1 mark)
   A. أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ
   B. الْمَاءُ مُفِيدٌ
   C. الْعَصِيرُ بَارِدٌ
   D. السَّمَكُ لَذِيذٌ

21. How does the Arabic comma ، differ from the English comma? (1 mark)
   A. It is a dot
   B. It is reversed
   C. It is bigger
   D. It is a line

22. Which Arabic sentence means "Water is useful (good for you)." (1 mark)
   A. السَّمَكُ لَذِيذٌ
   B. الْمَاءُ مُفِيدٌ
   C. أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ
   D. الْعَصِيرُ بَارِدٌ

23. What does the Arabic sentence الْمِفْتَاحُ فِي الْخِزَانَةِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The chair is at the door.
   B. The key is in the cupboard.
   C. Do not play with the knife.
   D. I read a book on Sunday.

24. What does the Arabic word حَمَّامٌ (hammaam) mean? (1 mark)
   A. cup
   B. chair
   C. spoon
   D. bathroom

25. Which of these letters does NOT join to the letter after it? (1 mark)
   A. ن (nuun)
   B. س (siin)
   C. ب (baa)
   D. ر (raa)

26. Which of these is a characteristic of good handwriting? (1 mark)
   A. Even spacing between words
   B. Large gaps inside a word
   C. Smudges
   D. Different sizes of letters

27. What does the Arabic word مِفْتَاحٌ (miftaah) mean? (1 mark)
   A. lamp
   B. key
   C. cup
   D. door

28. What does the Arabic word بَطْنٌ (batn) mean? (1 mark)
   A. mouth
   B. stomach
   C. hand
   D. finger

29. Which Arabic word means "tooth"? (1 mark)
   A. أُذُنٌ
   B. سِنٌّ
   C. رَأْسٌ
   D. وَجْهٌ

30. Which Arabic word means "beside"? (1 mark)
   A. بِجَانِبِ
   B. رِجْلٌ
   C. قَوِيٌّ
   D. أُمٌّ

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write five foods or drinks in Arabic (English letters are fine) with their meanings. (5 marks) (5 marks)

32. Translate into English: maa ismuki? (2 marks)

33. List four theme words about the home in Arabic (English letters), with meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)

34. Translate into English: haadhaa raʾsii (2 marks)

35. Write five words about weather and the environment in Arabic (English letters are fine) with their meanings. (5 marks) (5 marks)

36. Introduce yourself in Arabic (English letters are fine) with your name, that you are a pupil and that you are from Kenya, then give the English meaning. (4 marks) (4 marks)

37. Write a three-sentence paragraph about your room in Arabic sounds and give the meaning. (5 marks) (5 marks)

38. Explain why vocabulary building helps you to learn Arabic. (3 marks) (3 marks)

39. Translate into English: aktubu bi-yadii (2 marks)

40. Translate into English: haadhaa matar (2 marks)

41. Say why food is important for human life and name two foods grown in Kenya. (3 marks) (3 marks)

42. Translate into English: ʿindii akh wa ukht (2 marks)

43. Translate into English: aakulu l-khubza (2 marks)

44. Translate into English: fii l-matbakhi taawila wa kursii (2 marks)

45. Translate into English: haadhaa baytii (2 marks)

46. Give two ways of keeping household items safe. (2 marks) (2 marks)

47. Explain why writing the dots correctly is important. Give one example of two letters that differ only by dots. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — What is your name?
   maa ismuki? asks a girl for her name. The ending -ki is used for a girl.

2. C — أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ
   أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ (anaa bi-khayr) means I am well.

3. C — anaa
   أَنَا is read anaa and means I.

4. B — My brother plays.
   أَخِي يَلْعَبُ (akhii yalʿabu) means: My brother plays.

5. A — Sunday
   الْأَحَدُ (al-ahad) means Sunday.

6. A — Noticing the sounds inside words
   Phonological awareness is being aware of the separate sounds in words.

7. B — قِفْ
   قِفْ (qif) means stand up.

8. D — I speak with my mouth.
   أَتَكَلَّمُ بِفَمِي (atakallamu bi-famii) means: I speak with my mouth.

9. D — They act only on the correct instruction
   The game trains careful listening to instructions.

10. D — tree
   شَجَرَةٌ (shajara) means tree.

11. D — The weather is cold.
   الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ (al-jawwu baarid) means: The weather is cold.

12. B — In my house there is a kitchen.
   فِي بَيْتِي مَطْبَخٌ (fii baytii matbakh) means: In my house there is a kitchen.

13. A — bi
   بِ is read bi.

14. A — alif
   The letter ا is called alif.

15. C — The sound -an
   The double fatHa (tanwiin) gives the sound -an at the end of the word.

16. C — Cues
   Cues are clues such as pictures and the words around the new word.

17. A — alif, daal, dhaal, raa, zaay and waaw
   These six letters join only to the letter before them.

18. C — Hello, Ahmad.
   مَرْحَبًا يَا أَحْمَدُ (marhaban yaa Ahmad) means: Hello, Ahmad.

19. C — ath-thulaathaa'
   الثُّلَاثَاءُ is read ath-thulaathaa' and means Tuesday.

20. A — أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ
   أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ (uhibbu T-taʿaam) means: I like food.

21. B — It is reversed
   The Arabic comma and question mark are reversed because the script goes right to left.

22. B — الْمَاءُ مُفِيدٌ
   الْمَاءُ مُفِيدٌ (al-maa'u mufiid) means: Water is useful (good for you).

23. B — The key is in the cupboard.
   الْمِفْتَاحُ فِي الْخِزَانَةِ (al-miftaahu fii l-khizaana) means: The key is in the cupboard.

24. D — bathroom
   حَمَّامٌ (hammaam) means bathroom.

25. D — ر (raa)
   raa joins only to the letter before it. So do alif, daal, dhaal, zaay and waaw.

26. A — Even spacing between words
   Good handwriting has even spacing, correct shapes and neat presentation.

27. B — key
   مِفْتَاحٌ (miftaah) means key.

28. B — stomach
   بَطْنٌ (batn) means stomach.

29. B — سِنٌّ
   سِنٌّ (sinn) means tooth.

30. A — بِجَانِبِ
   بِجَانِبِ (bijaanibi) means beside.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example khubz (bread), aruzz (rice), dhura (maize), lahm (meat), samak (fish).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with its meaning.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: What is your name? (to a girl)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example bayt (house), matbakh (kitchen), taawila (table), kursii (chair).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my head.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example shams (sun), sahaab (clouds), matar (rain), riih (wind), samaa' (sky).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with its meaning.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: ismii Wanjiku. anaa tilmiidha. anaa min Kiiniya. My name is Wanjiku. I am a pupil. I am from Kenya.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence and 1 mark for the meaning.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example: haadhihi ghurfatii. fii l-ghurfati sariir. uhibbu ghurfatii. This is my room. In the room there is a bed. I like my room.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence, 1 mark for a beginning-middle-end order and 1 mark for the meaning.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: The more words you know, the more you can understand, say and write. Grouping words by theme helps you to remember them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for understanding, 1 mark for speaking or writing and 1 mark for remembering.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: I write with my hand.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is rain.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Food gives energy to grow, learn and stay healthy. Examples are maize and bananas.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the importance and 1 mark each for two foods.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: I have a brother and a sister.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: I eat bread.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: In the kitchen there is a table and a chair.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my house.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Keep the key in a safe place such as the cupboard; keep knives out of reach of small children; keep lamps away from water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each safe way.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: A wrong dot changes the letter and the word. For example ف has one dot above and ق has two dots above.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for changes the letter, 1 mark for changes the word, 1 mark for a correct example.
